BAGONG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City mvw.dilq.gov.ph OPINION NO. JUL 03 HON. FELIPE ANTONIO B. REMOLLO Mayor, City of Dumaguete City Hall Building, Sta. Catalina Street Dumaguete City Dear Mayor Dumaguete: This has reference to your letter dated February 1 , 2024, requesting this Department's legal opinion regarding the non-passage/non-approval of the Propose Annual Budget for CY 2024 of the City of Dumaguete despite the timely submission to the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of the 2024 Annual Investment Plan (AIP) on October II, 2023 and the proposed 2024 Annual Budget on October 13, 2023. Particularly, hereunder are the queries proffered: 1. Does the SP have the authority to change, alter, modify, or revise the duly passed and approved by the City Development Council (CDC)? 2. Does the SP have the authority to compel the City Mayor to convene the CDC full council for the purpose of changing, altering, modifying or revising the AIP that was already submitted to the SP on October II, 2023? 3. Can a newly constituted CDC full council (by reason of the inclusion of fifteen (15) new members while the tenure of office of the fifteen (15) original members ended due to October 30, 2023 Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections change, alter, revise or modify the AIP previously passed and approved by the previous CDC full council on October 9, 2023? 4. Is the submission of the 2024 AIP to the AP on October II, 2023, within the period prescribed by law, administrative issuances, and jurisprudence? 5. Is the submission of the 2024 Annual Budget to the SP on October 13, 2023, within the period prescribed by law, administrative issuances, and jurisprudence? And 6. Can the preparation and submission (October 13, 2023) of the 2024 Annual Budget to the SP be made while the latter is still deliberating on the AIP submitted on October 1 1 , 2023? Foremost, it is to be emphasized that central to the fiscal affairs of the local government units (LGUs) are the complementary roles of the Office of the Local Chief Executive (LCE) and the Sanggunian under the Local Government Code of 1991 (Republic Act No. 7160, hereinafter referred to as the Code) and other relevant laws. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Under the Code, the office of the LCE has the primary responsibility for the formulation of fiscal plans, such as the AIP and the Comprehensive Development Plan (CDP). Parenthetically, Section 109 of the Code mandates the Local Development Council (LDC), which is chaired by the LCE, to formulate the AIP. Having laid down the foregoing, we shall now answer the queries proffered in seriatim. On the first query. our opinion in DILG Opinion No. 22, Series of 2007 finds pertinent. Relevant portion of which reads: "[Bly statutory mandate, the formulation and initiation of the municipality's development plan is the primary function of the Municipal Development Council and the same has to be submitted to the Sangguniang Bayan for its appropriate action and approval the Sangguniang Bayan for its appropriate action and approval pursuant to Section 109 (a) in relation to Section 114 (a) of the Local Government Code of 1991. Such submission and approval are only for purposes of the enactment by the Sanggunian of the corresponding ordinance providing for legislative authorization of the budget for the proposed development projects consistent with the fundamental principle that no money shall be paid out of the local treasury except in pursuance of an appropriations ordinance (Section 305(a), Ibid). It must however be emphasized that although the Sangguniang Bayan is authorized by the Code to approve such municipal development plan formulated by the MDC only for the purpose as stated, such authority does not include the power to modify, revise or alter the same, albeit, the Sangguniang Bayan is not precluded from raising questions thereon for purposes of clarification. In out DILG Opinion No. 46, Series of 2002 dated March 18, 2002, we had the occasion to opine that, precisely, if the Sanqqunianq Bayan is not amenable to the MDC's approved projects and proqrams. the said sanqqunian should instead return it to the MDC with its comments and recommendations for LDC's proper consideration." (emphasis supplied) Further, in DILG Opinion No. 01, Series of 2008, the Department also opined that: "In this Department's previous opinions, we have consistently opined that the sanggunian's approval does not include the authority to revise the projects identified and formulated by the local development council since this would render nugatory the purposes and objectives for which local development councils had been institutionalized by the Code. If at all the sanggunian is not amenable to the LDC's approved projects and programs, the said sanggunian should instead return it to the LDC with its comments and recommendations and for the LDC's proper consideration. Hence, although the sanggunian is authorized by the Code to approve such policies, programs and projects formulated by the local development council, it cannot, however, modify, revise or alter the same." (emphasis supplied) Page 2 of 4

This Department has been consistent in its opinion that the Sangggunian has no authority to change, alter, modify, or revise the AIP duly passed and approved by the CDC. The role of the SP is essentially to approve the same, and it cannot revise the AIP as this would defeat the purposes and objectives institutionalized by the Code in establishing a CDC. It is to be noted, however, that the Sanggunian is not precluded from making recommendations on the AIP as it deems necessary, and subsequently referring back the same to the LCE for the latter's consideration. Going now to the second query, this Department is of the view that the Sanggunian is not clothed with the power to compel the City Mayor to convene the CDC full council for the purpose of changing, altering, modifying, or revising the AIP. The Code does not expressly mandate the LCE to convene the LDC as the sole mechanism for addressing the action undertaken by the sanggunian vis-å-vis the formulation and approval of the AIP. If the Sanggunian is not amenable to the submitted AIP, it should just return the same with suggestions or recommendations. Thereafter, it behooves the LCE to act on the recommendations or suggestions made by the sanggunian. As to the third query, the newly constituted CDC full council—resulting from the inclusion of fifteen (15) new members due to the October 30, 2023 Synchronized Barangay and Sangguniang Kabataan Elections—does not have the authority to change, alter, revise, or modify the AIP previously passed and approved by the previous CDC full council on October 9, 2023. To convene or not to convene the CDC in order to deal with the suggestions of the Sanggunian is not based on law. Mandamus may not lie. Hence, the Mayor cannot possibly be compelled or forced to convene the CDC, especially since the current CDC is practically new, with the replacement of about 15 Barangay Chairpersons after the October 2023 Barangay polls. Ordinarily, the CDC meets at least twice a year (Section 110, RA 7160). The preparation and approval of the AIP is understood to have been regular and above board. In the present case, the CDC unanimously approved the 2024 AIP. Therefore, convening the new CDC for the purpose of revising or modifying the AIP so as to accommodate the recommendations of the Sangguniang would be irregular since the work that would be revised is not the word of the current CDC but that of the previous one, whose inputs were based on the needs perceived by them to be paramount at that time. As to the fourth and fifth queries, the Department has issued Memorandum Circular No. 2022-004 to provide guidance on the timely submission and enactment of the LGU's annual appropriation budget, pertinent portion of which reads: "[All] LCEs, Vice-Mayors, and members of the Sanggunian are reminded on their compliance on the timelines and deadlines for the timely submissions and enactment of the annual budget, to wit: Activity Preparation of the Budget b the Local Legal Basis Section 318 of the LGC Page 3 of 4 Deadline October 16

Chief Executive Legislative Authorization ofthe Bud et Section 319 of the LGC December 31 Based on the foregoing, the submission of the 2024 AIP to the SP on October 11, 2023, in support of the 2024 Annual Budget, and the submission of the 2024 Annual Budget of the SP on October 13, 2023 are within the period prescribed and mandated by law and administrative issuances. As to the sixth query, this Department is of the opinion that while it may be ideal and procedurally sound that the formal or official submission of the Annual Budget to the Sanggunian should occur after the AIP has been approved, in practice there are significant procedural overlaps with this framework. Accordingly, the local finance committee may start preparing the Annual Budget—using the draft AIP as a reference—while the sanggunian is still deliberating on the AIP to obviate any practical and procedural overlaps and ultimately to ensure that there is no significant delay in the submission of the Annual Budget. Preliminary budget discussions may take place in parallel while the Sanggunian is still deliberating on the AIP. Stated succinctly, concurrent deliberations on both the Annual Budget and AIP may be done; in fact, it is practical to ensure that the Annual Budget and AIP are approved in a timely manner. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities or the courts. We hope to have guided you accordingly. Very truly yours, By the uthority of the Secretary: ATTY Un o OR R. LLAMAS cretary for Extemal, Legal and Legislative Affai JVRULLLS-LRALLD/jam Dir. LEOCADIO T.
